source_inventory.manifest_method: SHA-256 over sorted full path, mode, and Git blob inventory for each peeled release tree

workspace_boundary.thread_start: approvalPolicy=never; sandbox=workspace-write; cwd=the preflight-approved root; runtimeWorkspaceRoots contains only that same root
workspace_boundary.turn_start: sandboxPolicy.type=workspaceWrite; writableRoots contains only that same root; networkAccess=false; excludeSlashTmp=true; excludeTmpdirEnvVar=true
workspace_boundary.request_overlay: The adapter sends no config, trust, home, permission, windows.sandbox, windows.allow_mxc, MxC setup, application.network, path-alias, linked .git, or .aws write override.
workspace_boundary.meaning: The route supplies one unchanged host-approved root, keeps tool networkAccess=false and read-only defaults, and leaves Codex-managed provider, filesystem, bootstrap-proxy, Windows sandbox, and application-network policies in force; no Windows runtime-isolation claim is made.

selected_route.failure_projection: The driver ignores provider-specific error details; request errors become request_failed, turn status failed becomes a generic ProviderFailed terminal, and notifications are not upgraded into success from error payloads.

hops.classification: The selected thread/start trust path skips automatic persisted Trusted state for projectless layer stacks; marked roots retain the existing path. Selected model/list and turn/start now revalidate managed model-provider requirements and reject a changed selection/definition or requirement load error before provider work. Permission materialization fails closed for home-relative denials without a home fact and for invalid workspace globs; the fallback can remove all write grants. Default-enabled SystemProxyFallback adds a safe-to-replay bootstrap GET retry through the host system proxy after connect/timeout failures. Explicit ambient windows.sandbox=mxc can select the new Windows MxC tool backend; the adapter sends no such config or setup RPC. Local thread-store changes add cancellation-owned startup persistence and delete local agent message-board data before hard-deleting rollouts. Selected required wire fields stay present; optional additions and unselected RPCs remain unmapped.
hops.disposition: Qualified under Contract 023 decisions d7dbacde-6381-47c5-8255-6729d309b147 and d9a1fe6e-6481-433c-b643-ada177613e07. The route preserves the exact approved-root request and generic refusals; managed provider checks, fail-closed permissions, bootstrap proxy policy, and explicitly configured MxC remain provider-owned and are never bypassed.

hops.classification: This hop adds system, device-management, and cloud application.network destination restrictions to Codex app-server provider/API HTTP traffic, with local policy loaded before cloud access and failed local policy loads failing closed. This is distinct from the adapter's turn/start sandboxPolicy.networkAccess=false for tool sandbox access.
hops.disposition: Qualified under Contract 023 decision d9a1fe6e-6481-433c-b643-ada177613e07. Host-managed application.network policy governs provider/API HTTP independently of the selected tool sandbox networkAccess=false; exact route tests retain false and send no application.network override.

hops.classification: The permission source normalizes path aliases and accounts for linked .git targets as read-only carveouts inside a broader writable root; it does not grant access beyond the selected root. A new approval helper is not selected because this route observes and stops provider approval requests. CodexErrorInfo adds an error variant; the adapter projects failures generically.
hops.disposition: Contract 023 decision d7dbacde-6381-47c5-8255-6729d309b147 authorizes the bounded alias and linked-.git behavior; selected-route fixtures now assert those root inputs do not expand the one approved workspace root.

hops.classification: Codex adds an existing top-level <writable-root>/.aws directory to its default read-only subpaths. Its frozen regression tests show a normal src/main.rs path remains writable while a write to .aws/config is denied; the rationale is to block credential-helper execution. The adapter still sends exactly one approved root and no .aws write exception. The turn error enum/text changes do not change the selected status/error shape used by the adapter.
hops.disposition: Contract 023 decision cb18500a-499a-4cbe-ae1b-8daec34d5ebe accepts this exact read-only carveout. Document it as a version-specific workspace-write limitation; do not restore writes. Contract 036 patch compatibility remains for planner review.

hops.classification: The app-server tracks running-turn count incrementally instead of recomputing it from thread runtime state. Its upstream regression covers simultaneous turns, duplicate start notifications, thread removal, and emitted count values; the selected status values remain the same. Content-filter errors are still represented as failed turns and mapped to the route's generic provider failure.

hops.classification: Selected thread/resume now pairs persisted snapshots with file revisions and reuses them only if the exact rollout revision still matches after writer acquisition; otherwise the store reloads authoritative history. History projection reads run in one blocking task and preserve the newline-terminated durable prefix. A selected resume also serializes with internal thread-goal resume work; goal mutation methods and prediction notifications remain unselected. On Windows, explicit MxC selection now passes through managed windows.sandbox constraints and the local prefer_mxc feature is gated by that policy; this stays within the explicit ambient MxC boundary accepted by decision d9a1fe6e-6481-433c-b643-ada177613e07. Unknown CodexErrorInfo variants remain ignored by the adapter, and selected required thread/turn wire fields stay present.
hops.disposition: History snapshot revision validation and refresh remain compatible within the selected thread/resume surface. Explicit MxC remains accepted only under the approved host/resource and managed-policy limits in decision d9a1fe6e-6481-433c-b643-ada177613e07; no adapter setup, bypass, root expansion, or Windows runtime-isolation claim is made.
